sections.content: You know *llevar* + time + gerund from the first lesson of this unit: *Llevo tres años trabajando aquí*. *Venir* + gerund also says that something began in the past and goes on until now, but it looks back along the whole way: the speaker sees a process that has built up, or a habit that has kept repeating. It is common in news, reports and speeches: *Los precios vienen subiendo desde hace meses*. It often goes with *desde*, *desde hace*, *últimamente* or *año tras año*, and it does not count the time. *Venir* can also be in the imperfect: *Veníamos hablando de eso cuando llegó Ana*.
sections.title: Looking back along the way
venir + gerund
rows: Los precios vienen subiendo desde hace varios meses.
Prices have been going up for several months.
Vengo pensando en cambiar de trabajo desde el verano.
I have been thinking about changing jobs since the summer.
Esta empresa viene creciendo año tras año.
This company has been growing year after year.
Veníamos hablando de eso cuando llegó Ana.
We had been talking about that when Ana arrived.

sections.content: *Llevar* counts the time and *venir* follows the process. You say *Llevo tres años pensando en eso*, with the number of years, but *Vengo pensando en eso desde hace tiempo*, without counting. Do not put a counted length of time right after *venir*: not *Vengo tres años pensando*.
